blocks.text: Seth pulled against the cuffs again.

He tried to settle his grip against one edge and concentrate. Then the chair rattled as he jerked with his shoulders instead. Steel pressed into his wrists, and the room seemed to tilt. He stopped before the dizziness grew worse.

Beside him, Jenny blinked against the ache behind her eyes. Her hands were still fastened to the arms of her chair and her ankles locked against its legs. Across the room, Fist lay at the bottom of the bird cage. His torn white cuff shifted as he tried to rise.
“Easy,” Jenny said quietly.
“I can bend these.” Seth looked down at his red gloves. “I should be able to.”
“You’ve still got that stuff in your head.”
He swallowed and rested against the metal backing. The cuffs stayed shut.
blocks.alt: Seth rests against his chair while Jenny watches him with concern. Both remain secured by steel wrist and ankle cuffs; injured Fist lies inside one locked bird cage on the bench.

blocks.text: Daniel gave the fastening at Seth’s right wrist another tug. Then he stepped back, looking pleased with himself.
“There. Both of you can save yourselves some trouble.”
Luke hovered over the workbench. “And now?”
Daniel turned toward him. “Now I can get some work done.”
“On my body?”
“That is what you wanted, isn’t it?”
Luke drifted closer to Seth’s chair. Seth watched the iron teeth until Luke turned back toward his uncle.
“You said you needed him. You’ve got him.”
Daniel walked to the collector. A loose wire hung beneath its frame. He lifted it, checked its end, and laid it across the bench.
“There are other things to consider.”
“Like the fireball.”
Daniel reached for a screwdriver.
“You haven’t caught him,” Luke said.
“I can see that.”
“And this isn’t finished.”
Daniel put the screwdriver down harder than he needed to. A beaker rattled against a jar.
Jenny watched his hands. He had checked their cuffs twice, but he had not connected anything to either chair. The collector stood empty.
“You don’t know what to do next,” she said.
He looked sharply at her. “You came here to ask about electricity, Miss Jenkins. You’ve had your demonstration.”
“I’ve had gas blown in my face. So has he.”
“And he would have wrecked my laboratory if I hadn’t stopped him.”
Seth lifted his head. “Let her go.”
Daniel moved a bundle of papers away from the collector, searching beneath them. “You’re hardly in a position to give orders.”
“She hasn’t done anything to you.”
Daniel found his pencil. He pulled a sheet toward him and began drawing. Jenny looked at Seth, then at the glass booth beyond the benches. Seth followed her gaze.
He remembered the hiss from the vents. His fingers loosened around the edge of the cuff.
Across the room, Fist pushed himself a few inches above the cage floor. He tipped to one side and settled back down.
Luke looked over.
“Still here,” Fist muttered.
“You’ll stay there.”
“Come closer and say that.”
Luke started toward the cage.
“Leave it alone,” Daniel said. “I need to think.”
Luke stopped. He looked from the glove to his uncle, who was rubbing out a line on the paper.
blocks.alt: Daniel erases a line from his diagram as impatient Luke hovers beside him. The unfinished glass collector stands empty with disconnected wires.

blocks.text: Jenny tested one ankle restraint while their attention was elsewhere. The steel held her leg against the chair, but she could move the toe of her shoe a little. She tried the other foot, then let both settle.
Seth noticed. She gave him a small shake of her head.
Not yet.
He took a slow breath and fixed his attention on the edge beneath his gloved fingers. Then Daniel moved behind Jenny’s chair, and Seth’s attention went with him.
Daniel checked her wrist cuffs. Jenny held still until he let go.
“Billy knows where I am,” she said.
“I’ve spoken to Billy.”
“Then you know he won’t just wait for me to come back.”
Daniel glanced at the workshop doorway.
Luke rose a little. “Do you want me outside again?”
“No.” Daniel looked toward the small window high in the basement wall, then back at the chairs. “Stay here for now.”
He returned to the bench and drew another line. Luke followed him.
“You told me you could put me right.”
“And I will need more than five minutes without you interrupting me.”
“I caught the glove. I kept out of the way when the boy came in. What else do you want me to do?”
Daniel’s pencil stopped. He stared at the unfinished collector.
“Let me work it out.”
Seth looked toward the doorway. He had been supposed to wait there for Billy. Instead, he had run straight past the bench as soon as he saw Jenny.
Now Billy would arrive without knowing what had happened.
“He’ll be careful,” Jenny whispered.
Seth looked back at her. She had seen where he was looking.
He wanted to believe her. He pressed his gloved hand flat against the armrest and tried to keep still.
Outside, Billy waited at a crossing while a delivery truck lumbered past. He stepped off the curb as soon as the way was clear.

He had reported Jenny missing and left to meet Seth. On the way, the Blackwells’ limousine had drawn alongside him. Claude had offered a ride, and Billy had accepted reluctantly. It should have been quicker than walking.

Eleanor had asked whether he was still calling on Daniel. With Claude beside her, Billy had kept his answer short. The invoice proved she had paid the rent. It did not prove she had knowingly paid for the robot, or given the order that held back the police.

Then came a quick stop at her campaign office for some papers. One packet had become another, and Eleanor had found another question while the driver waited. Billy had asked twice to be taken straight to his appointment. Claude had apologized for the delay and offered to drop him nearer, but Billy had finally got out two streets short and set off on foot. Seth should be waiting by the yard steps, and Fist should have something to tell them.
Billy looked up at the rooftops. There was no red glove above the street.
He walked faster.
Inside the laboratory, Daniel laid his pencil down. He looked from Seth to the empty collector. Luke hovered beside him, waiting.
“Well?” Luke demanded.
Daniel took off his glasses and wiped them on his coat.
Outside, Billy turned onto the laboratory’s street.
blocks.alt: Billy, in his plaid deerstalker and high-collared tan trench coat, walks around a Cleveland street corner toward the laboratory, looking up at the empty rooftops.
